newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges up to 9.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges up to 9.2 percent.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged up 20 basis points to 9.2 percent, boosted by longer-term bank borrowings at higher rates.
Total settlements reached 32.8 million kuna, leaving a 4.2 million kuna surplus on the supply side.
Dealers put new borrowings at 25 million kuna. Call money rates were slightly higher at 9.0-9.5 percent. One long-term loan was struck at 15 percent.
Insusrers' previous loans were extended at a steady 8.0 percent.
Overnight trade totalled 80 million kuna, which was enirely used to cover one bank's mandatory reserve.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Wednesday eased to 5.4684 agaist the dollar and to 3.5599 to the German mark. --Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
